Gaslamp halos string themselves along the gantry rails, each globe blurred soft by the harbor fog rolling in off the bay.
Dawn breaks amber and slow over the moored fleet, mist clinging to the docking cradles, every hull edged in quiet gold.
The ships' running-lights kindle one by one as dusk thickens, small warm points strung through the cooling blue air of the harbor.
Fog moves through the mooring-masts in slow grey curtains, the gaslamps below burning steady gold against the damp and the dark.
A low amber sunset spreads behind the docked airships, their silhouettes sharp and enormous against the burning western sky.
Rain slicks the quayside stones to mirrors, every lampost doubling itself in long amber columns across the wet cobbles.
Searchlight beams sweep wide arcs through the harbor fog, catching nothing but pale drift and the brief glitter of wet rigging.
A hundred gondola-windows glow warm at twilight, the moored fleet a constellation of amber light suspended above the darkening docks.
The brass gantries catch the last of the sunset and hold it, warm metal shining through threads of drifting harbor mist.
Morning fog lies thick across the lower berths, gaslamps burning patient and gold through the grey, the fleet barely visible beyond.
Blue dusk settles cold and clear above the harbor, the running-lights of the great ships mirrored faint in the water far below.
Lamplit fog rolls slow between the mooring-masts, softening every edge, turning the whole sky-harbor into something luminous and half-dreamed.
The quay shines after rain, lamp-glow pooled in every hollow of the stones, the moored hulls dark and dripping overhead.
Searchlights rake the fogbank above the outer berths, crossing and uncrossing, finding only depth and more pale grey beyond.
Gondola-windows at dusk burn like lanterns in a slow procession, the moored airships glowing from within against the fading harbor sky.
A golden dawn rims the high mooring-masts in fire, the lower docks still drowned in blue shadow and pooling morning mist.
Harbor fog catches the gaslamp light and holds it, making soft amber globes of each lamp along the gantry walk.
The running-lights come on at dusk in silence, one ship then the next, threading warm color through the cooling harbor air.
Sunset silhouettes the docked fleet in a single dark mass, their fins and envelopes enormous against the amber western glow.
Rain on the quayside turns every lamp into a smeared reflection, the whole harbor front shimmering and doubled in the wet.
Searchlight beams swing slowly across the fog, each beam solid as a pillar for a moment before the mist swallows it.
Twilight deepens over the harbor and the gondola-windows warm against it, a low galaxy of amber light among the moored ships.
Gaslamps along the lower gantries hold their glow steady in the fog, a brass-warm corridor threading through the grey damp air.
The dawn comes up slow and gold behind the fleet, mist burning off the envelope fabric in long pale wisps of steam.
Dusk turns the harbor a deep and luminous blue, the running-lights of a dozen moored ships kindling soft against the cold air.
